title: Double-Angle Formulas
short: sin 2θ = 2 sin θ cos θ and three forms of cos 2θ.

blocks.html: Put $\beta = \alpha$ in the sum formulas and you get formulas for twice an angle. They show up all over calculus and physics, so they are worth knowing on sight.

$$\sin(\theta + \theta) = \sin\theta\cos\theta + \cos\theta\sin\theta = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta,$$ and $\cos(\theta + \theta) = \cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta$. Replace $\sin^2\theta$ with $1 - \cos^2\theta$ to get $2\cos^2\theta - 1$, or replace $\cos^2\theta$ with $1 - \sin^2\theta$ to get $1 - 2\sin^2\theta$. Three forms of one fact; pick the one that matches what you know.

blocks.name: graph
blocks.cap: $\sin 2x$ (solid) squeezes the wave; $2\sin x$ (dashed) stretches it. They are different functions.

blocks.title: From one value
blocks.q: $\sin\theta = \frac{3}{5}$ and $\theta$ is in Quadrant II. Find $\sin 2\theta$ and $\cos 2\theta$.
steps: First $\cos\theta$: $\cos^2\theta = 1 - \frac{9}{25} = \frac{16}{25}$, and cosine is negative in Quadrant II, so $\cos\theta = -\frac{4}{5}$.

blocks.title: Choosing the form
steps: Only cosine is given, so use $\cos 2\theta = 2\cos^2\theta - 1$.

blocks.html: Writing $\sin 2\theta = 2\sin\theta$. Doubling the angle does not double the value. Check with $\theta = 90^\circ$: $\sin 180^\circ = 0$, but $2\sin 90^\circ = 2$. (Sine values never exceed $1$, so $2\sin\theta$ cannot be a sine.)
